newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares edge lower in listless late trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares edge lower in listless late trade.

text.p: German shares fell in afternoon electronic trade on Tuesday, lacking the impetus to continue recent gains in the absence of any new indicators and with a lower Wall Street start weighing on sentiment.
The IBIS DAX index was down 30.15 points, or 0.80 percent, at 3,719.87 points in the afternoon, while the June DAX future was down 27 points at 3,721 points.
The Dow Jones index was down around 30 points at 7,744.04 points in early trade. Stocks had been expected to open steady after U.S. Consumer Price Index data came in line with analysts' expectations.
Dealers said that market sentiment was generally nervous. "This market needs a rest," said one trader, who said the bullish mode of recent weeks was taking a toll.
Most of the gains early in the day were derivative-based, which made for greater levels of volatility.
"A lot of the movement is being led by the future, so you don't want to read too much into it. Don't forget we've got the triple-witching on Friday," the trader said.
Also contributing to jitters were market concerns about the effectiveness of the stability pact agreed at the Amsterdam summit.
EU leaders on Monday agreed to a resolution on employment to accompany the stability pact, the framework for securing fiscal discipline after the start of European currency union.
Builders Hochtief and Holzmann were down around four percent each on cyclical reasons, dealers said.
